content:
incident-bot: Incident created: HIGH - unexpected model warmup failures and node flaps in us-west-2. Paging @jordan (oncall) and @sarah (sre). Alerts show spikes in 5xx for /v1/generate and repeated model-load OOMs on several GPU nodes.

jordan (oncall): I'm on it. what's the scope? any customer-facing outages?

anya (support): customers reporting 503s on cold starts. support queue up ~20 tickets; two flagged as enterprise-impact. error samples reference 'model warmup timed out' and 'internal server error'.

sarah (sre): pulling logs. multiple pods in CrashLoopBackOff during warmup, all on nodes in gpu-pool-b. common pattern: deserialization error followed by cuda allocation failure.

sarah (sre): paste logs:
```
[2026-03-15T22:10:02Z] warmup: deserializing weights shard=0 error="unexpected EOF while reading"
[2026-03-15T22:10:03Z] runtime: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
[2026-03-15T22:10:03Z] kubelet: container exited with code 137
```

mike (eng-runtime): interesting, EOF suggests possible artifact corruption or partial download. but cuda OOM right after could be memory spike during fallback compile. did we just push a model variant?

paul (mlops): yes, a canary of model-x v2026-03-15 was rolled out at 22:00 UTC to us-west-2 canary group. It increased total params due to new attention block, ~10% larger. registry shows artifact checksum matches upload.

kevin (infra): I'm seeing IO errors in the pod logs when fetching model shards from our artifact store for a subset of nodes (sustained 500s from blobstore near az2). could be transient network/storage flakiness causing corrupted downloads.

jordan (oncall): immediately: 1) stop canary routing; 2) disable warmup for v2026-03-15; 3) cordon/evict the affected nodes to avoid cascading restarts. mike, can you flip routing?

mike (eng-runtime): doing route revert: `redwood route set --model model-x --from canary=v2026-03-15 --to stable=v2026-02-28 --region us-west-2`

mike (eng-runtime): disabling warmup prefetch for that variant: `redwood config set --model model-x --variant v2026-03-15 --warmup.enabled=false --region us-west-2`

incident-bot: Status changed to INVESTIGATING -> MITIGATED (partial). Routing reverted; warmup disabled; artifact store team alerted.

kevin (infra): cordon and drain started on nodes showing repeated blobstore 500s: `kubectl cordon gpu-b-03 && kubectl drain gpu-b-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

paul (mlops): note: if downloads are corrupted due to storage, we should ensure model checksum verification happens before attempting to mmap or deserialize. current warmup path assumes downloads succeed. adding checksum verify pre-deserialize as a short-term fix.

sarah (sre): meanwhile some pods remain in CrashLoopBackOff due to OOM at load. draining nodes will help but we should avoid bulk restart of warmups. can we temporarily reduce warmup concurrency globally?

mike (eng-runtime): lowering warmup concurrency in us-west-2 from 4 -> 1: `redwood config set --fleet us-west-2 --warmup.concurrency=1`

mike (eng-runtime): also applying a compile guard to abort warmup early if compile-duration > 30s to prevent memory pressure from long-running kernel compiles. pushing small hotfix to runtime canary.

jordan (oncall): kevin, any risk that draining these nodes will trigger autoscaler to spin up new nodes that also hit the storage issue?

kevin (infra): autoscaler will provision new nodes from same AZ. I'm gating node replacement until storage errors clear. I'm adding a placement filter: `--avoid-az az2` for new node provisioning temporarily.

anya (support): updating customers: "We're aware of some 5xx and 503 errors for cold starts in us-west-2. We've routed traffic away from the canary model and are investigating model warmup failures and storage errors impacting artifact fetches. We'll update within 60 minutes."

incident-bot: Noted: storage team assigned.

storage-team-bot: investigating blobstore 500s in az2. seeing spike in tail latency and a small number of corrupted ranges. rolling forward redundant replicas for impacted ranges.

paul (mlops): adding quick checksum verification step to the warmup path. if checksum fails, abort and mark artifact as failed to fetch (don't attempt to deserialize). will submit PR now.

mike (eng-runtime): PR submitted for compile-time abort and checksum gating: https://git.internal/redwood/eng-runtime/pull/3930. applying to canary.

kevin (infra): node gpu-b-03 drained and rebooted. after reboot, kubelet shows healthy and no more immediate OOMs. but I'm seeing kernel messages indicating occasional driver reset on a different node gpu-b-07. escalating to hardware vendor.

sarah (sre): after routing revert and concurrency reduction, 5xx rates dropped to baseline. however warmup errors still present in logs for prior failed pods. need to verify no customer request still hitting canary.

mike (eng-runtime): verified: gateway routing table shows 100% to stable variant. no active sessions to canary.

incident-bot: Status updated: MITIGATED.

jordan (oncall): next steps: - storage: remediate corrupted ranges and verify blobstore health; - eng-runtime: add checksum pre-deserialize and compile abort guard; - mlops: halt the v2026-03-15 rollout and mark artifact for re-upload if checksum issues persist; - infra: monitor gpu pool for driver resets and avoid az2 for new placement until cleared; - support: customer comms and ticket handling. assign owners accordingly.

paul (mlops): halting rollout and disabling automatic re-deploy for that artifact until we confirm artifact integrity across regions.

mike (eng-runtime): adding telemetry to capture transient memory spikes during compile fallback and warmup to better alert on OOM risk. Also adding abort condition where estimated_live_mem + compile_peak_estimate > 0.9 * gpu_mem.

kevin (infra): vendor replied: possible thermal throttling causing occasional driver resets; we've scheduled a patch window for the cluster's firmware in az2 tomorrow. for now avoiding new placements in az2.

anya (support): posted customer follow-up: "Root cause appears to be a combination of artifact fetch corruption from blobstore in az2 and a newly rolled model with higher memory profile, which together caused warmup OOMs and 5xx for cold starts. We reverted routing and mitigated impact; a postmortem will follow."

sarah (sre): preparing postmortem, collecting timelines, logs, and affected customers. will include queries to identify exact number of affected requests and tenants. target to publish within 24 hours.

jordan (oncall): moving to monitoring mode for 3 hours. reopen if anything regresses. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
